text.insert: Seed the knowledge base by running the initial librarian backfill over prepared sources and game targets. The librarian researches each target and proposes cited facts and relationships. Validation controls what is stored. Complete build and sandbox readiness checks before starting Run.
Review Standards Before Backfill

Review the accepted baseline standards before starting librarian backfill. Librarian context includes standards for recognizing authored rules. Standards are not citable knowledge. After seeding, review additions and revisions against the available evidence before starting Run.
Standards
describes the current record format and enforcement. Explicit global/game scope and composition are proposed; do not assume game-specific overrides are implemented.

Before launching kg2-backfill, review the selected game's config/backfill.json. With schemaVersion 1, this optional file supplies provider, model, thinkingLevel, concurrency, limit, and agentTimeoutSeconds defaults for that command. Explicit CLI flags override the file. Other jobs keep their own settings. A configured limit bounds each invocation. Raising concurrency does not remove that limit. Increase concurrency between measured batches after reviewing completed passes, failures, rate limits, and citation quality. The loader does not automatically ramp concurrency.

If a response cannot be parsed as a JSON object, backfill makes one correction call with the original output and parser error, provided time remains. That call keeps the selected model and research context, shares the original time budget and concurrency slot, and preserves separate output artifacts. A second parse failure fails the pass. Corrected proposals still pass envelope, citation, and scope validation before storage.

steps.text: Verify initial Sync and prepared sources
Require accepted checkout and build evidence, extracted targets, verified captures, and working indexes. Verify embeddings separately from keyword-index readiness.
Research the selected targets using the prepared records and code evidence. Validate proposals and resolve citations before writing knowledge.
Record completed targets, failed passes, unavailable resources, and subjects with no supported facts. Retry failed work without treating absence of evidence as a failed pass.
Compare the sandbox build with the accepted host build and preserve execution evidence.
Require all configured gates. Record any pending optional curation explicitly and retain the accepted head and initial save point.

text.insert: Verify analysis graph inputs before backfill. The graph rebuild job supplies the selected game's report path, knowledge root, and Ghidra/opseq index roots to those builders. Each registered source needs its own source.json descriptor. For SMS, rebuild the supported code_graph, ghidra_xrefs, opseq_similarity, and decomp_standards sources explicitly, then inspect indexed_sources and skipped_sources. Other legacy graph builders are not covered by this path verification. A graph export alone does not establish semantic curation or sandbox readiness.

Sync publication passes the resolved game's runtime database path into attempt intake. The knowledge directory does not determine the Harness State location. During onboarding, inspect the published Sync result and readiness fields before launching backfill; a validated build can still be followed by a publication or source-intake failure. Recover a failed Sync through its recorded state rather than treating partial imports as a completed save point.

Bootstrap requires declared source acquisition, import, and search indexes, plus mechanical entities and valid build evidence. Semantic curation can remain pending with visible coverage. Sandbox readiness requires separate verified execution evidence before Run admission.
Sandbox Readiness

Initial Sync accepts the configured checkout and build evidence before sandbox validation. The validation command reserves exclusive dispatch authority, checks the accepted head and configuration, builds host and Daytona reports, compares scored functions and sizes, preserves evidence, and deletes the sandbox. Only successful validation marks sandbox readiness ready. Initial readiness is recorded when every required gate is ready.
bun run server:job -- validate-sandbox --game <id> [--sandbox-profile <name>]
Evidence lives under the resolved game state directory at
sandbox-validation/<operation>/

. It records host and remote reports, profile, image, accepted head, configuration, and build output. This operation contacts Daytona. Configuration tests alone do not satisfy the gate, and no live validation is implied by a registered descriptor.

To review the first epoch before running workers, complete Sync and sandbox validation, then create the Run record with init-run --game <id> and seed it with prepare-epoch --game <id>. Omit --epoch-target-cap to include every eligible open target. Verify Harness State remains paused and Dispatch State has no active lease. Preparation does not start a process.
Worktree Handoff

Harness State owns the canonical worktree and source lineage. Sync owns upstream intake, staging, validation, and confirmed publication. Descriptor resolution alone does not establish bootstrap readiness.
Configure Standards
is the next setup step. Use the seeded knowledge to review game requirements or changes to shared rules. Then verify their instructions and checks before Run.
